projectCategory: DSA Module 9.2: Quick Sort & Merge Sort Architecture
subject: Data Structures & Algorithms in C

projects.title: Standard Merge Sort (Divide & Conquer Subarray Merging)
projects.description: Merge Sort is a classic Divide and Conquer algorithm. Recursively divides array into two halves until single-element subfiles are reached, then merges two sorted subarrays using an auxiliary buffer `O(N)`. Guarantees optimal `O(N log N)` time in ALL cases (worst, average, best) and is STABLE! In this project, you will build Merge Sort Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Divide & Conquer Subarray Merges, Guaranteed O(N log N) Bounds & Auxiliary Buffer Transfers
projects.exampleText: Sort array [38, 27, 43, 3, 9, 82, 10] using Merge Sort
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Standard Merge Sort ---
Sorted Array: 3 9 10 27 38 43 82
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Divide**: Find midpoint `m = l + (r - l) / 2`; recurse on `l..m` and `m+1..r`.
2. **Conquer Merge**: Merge sorted subarrays using auxiliary buffer `L` and `R`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `merge_sort()`: Solves array sorting using Standard Merge Sort.

projects.title: In-Place Merge Sort (Minimal Auxiliary Array Transfers)
projects.description: In-Place Merge Sort merges two sorted adjacent subarrays without allocating dynamic heap buffers. Shifts elements rightward in-place or rotates subarrays to maintain sorted order in `O(1)` extra memory! In this project, you will build In-Place Merge Sort in C.
projects.learningOutcome: In-Place Subarray Merging, Memory Transfer Reduction & Subarray Shift Rotations
projects.exampleText: Merge sorted adjacent subarrays in-place
projects.exampleOutput:
--- In-Place Merge Sort ---
Merged sorted subarrays in-place with minimal memory transfers.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Pointer Traversal**: Track `i` in left subarray, `j` in right subarray.
2. **In-Place Shift**: If `arr[j] < arr[i]`, shift element rightward to insert `arr[j]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `inplace_merge_sort_demo()`: Solves In-Place Merge Sort.

projects.title: Iterative Bottom-Up Merge Sort (Non-Recursive Subarray Merging)
projects.description: Iterative Bottom-Up Merge Sort eliminates function call stack recursion overhead. Merges subfiles of size `width = 1`, then `width = 2`, `4`, `8...` up to `N` using simple loops in `O(N log N)` time and `O(1)` call stack memory! In this project, you will build Bottom-Up Merge Sort Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Iterative Subfile Merges, Stack-Free Merge Passes & Power-of-2 Width Expansion
projects.exampleText: Sort array iteratively without recursion stack using width sizes 1, 2, 4, 8...
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Iterative Bottom-Up Merge Sort ---
Sorted array iteratively using width sizes 1, 2, 4, 8... without recursion stack.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Width Outer Loop**: Loop `width` doubling from 1 to N.
2. **Subarray Merges**: Merge pairs of subarrays `[i .. i+width-1]` and `[i+width .. i+2*width-1]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `iterative_merge_sort_demo()`: Solves Iterative Bottom-Up Merge Sort.

projects.title: Standard Quick Sort (Lomuto Partition Scheme)
projects.description: Quick Sort selects a pivot element (Lomuto picks `arr[high]`) and partitions array into elements `<= pivot` and `> pivot`. Recursively sorts partitions in-place in average `O(N log N)` time and `O(1)` extra memory! In this project, you will build Lomuto Quick Sort Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: QuickSort Lomuto Partitioning, Pivot Element Placement & In-Place Array Division
projects.exampleText: Sort array [10, 7, 8, 9, 1, 5] using Lomuto Quick Sort
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Standard Quick Sort (Lomuto Partition) ---
Sorted Array: 1 5 7 8 9 10
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Lomuto Partition**: Pick `pivot = arr[high]`; scan `j` from `low` to `high-1`.
2. **Pivot Index**: Swap elements `<=` pivot to left side; place pivot at `i+1`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `quick_sort_lomuto()`: Solves array sorting using Lomuto Partition Quick Sort.

projects.title: Quick Sort with Hoare's Partition Scheme
projects.description: Hoare's Partition Scheme uses two pointers scanning from `low` (left to right) and `high` (right to left), swapping elements out of order. Performs 3x FEWER swaps than Lomuto Scheme on average! In this project, you will build Hoare Quick Sort Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Hoare Dual Pointer Partitioning, Reduced Swap Operations & QuickSort Variants
projects.exampleText: Sort array using Hoare's Partition Scheme
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Quick Sort with Hoare's Partition Scheme ---
Partitioned array with fewer swaps than Lomuto scheme.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Dual Pointers**: Increment `i` while `arr[i] < pivot`; decrement `j` while `arr[j] > pivot`.
2. **Pointer Swap**: Swap `arr[i]` and `arr[j]` until pointers cross.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `hoare_partition_demo()`: Solves Quick Sort using Hoare's Partition Scheme.

projects.title: Randomized Quick Sort (Random Pivot Selection)
projects.description: Standard Quick Sort degrades to `O(N^2)` worst-case on sorted inputs when choosing fixed pivots. Randomized Quick Sort selects a RANDOM element in `low..high` as pivot, guaranteeing EXPECTED `O(N log N)` runtime regardless of adversary inputs! In this project, you will build Randomized Quick Sort Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Random Pivot Selection, Adversary Resistance & Expected O(N log N) Guarantees
projects.exampleText: Sort array using Randomized Quick Sort
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Randomized Quick Sort ---
Selected random pivots to guarantee expected O(N log N) time on adversary inputs.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Random Pivot**: Pick `pivot_idx = low + rand() % (high - low + 1)`.
2. **Swap to End**: Swap `arr[pivot_idx]` with `arr[high]`; run standard partition.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `randomized_quicksort_demo()`: Solves Randomized Quick Sort.

projects.title: Median-of-Three Pivot Selection Quick Sort
projects.description: Select pivot as the MEDIAN of three elements: `first = arr[low]`, `middle = arr[mid]`, and `last = arr[high]`. Avoids `O(N^2)` behavior on sorted, reverse-sorted, and nearly-sorted arrays without random number generation calls! In this project, you will build Median-of-Three Quick Sort in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Median-of-Three Heuristics, Pivot Selection Optimization & Sorting Protection
projects.exampleText: Sort array picking median of first, middle, and last elements as pivot
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Median-of-Three Pivot Selection Quick Sort ---
Picked median of first, middle, and last elements as pivot.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Median Selection**: Compare `arr[low]`, `arr[mid]`, `arr[high]`; pick median value.
2. **Pivot Placement**: Swap median element into `arr[high]` before partitioning.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `median_of_three_quicksort_demo()`: Solves Quick Sort using Median-of-Three pivot selection.

projects.title: Merge Sort for Singly Linked List
projects.description: Merge Sort is the PREFERRED algorithm for sorting Singly Linked Lists! Uses Fast/Slow Pointers to split list at midpoint in `O(N)` without array indexing, and merges lists via pointer rewiring in `O(N log N)` time and `O(log N)` stack space! In this project, you will build Linked List Merge Sort in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Linked List Merge Sort, Fast/Slow Pointer Midpoint Splitting & Pointer Rewiring
projects.exampleText: Sort singly linked list in O(N log N) time via Merge Sort
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Merge Sort for Singly Linked List ---
Sorted singly linked list in O(N log N) time and O(log N) stack space using Fast/Slow pointers.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Fast/Slow Split**: Use `slow` and `fast` pointers to split list in half.
2. **Pointer Merge**: Recursively sort halves and merge by updating `next` pointers.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `linked_list_merge_sort_demo()`: Solves Merge Sort for Singly Linked List.

projects.title: Count Inversions in Array using Merge Sort in O(N log N)
projects.description: An inversion is a pair `(i, j)` where `i < j` and `arr[i] > arr[j]`. During the merge step of Merge Sort, if `L[i] > R[j]`, then ALL remaining elements in `L` from `i` to `mid` form inversions with `R[j]`! Counts total inversions in `O(N log N)` time instead of naive `O(N^2)`. In this project, you will build Merge Inversion Counter in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Array Inversion Counting, Merge Sort Cross-Half Inversions & O(N log N) Math Proofs
projects.exampleText: Count inversions for [8, 4, 2, 1] using Merge Sort
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Count Inversions using Merge Sort ---
Total Inversions in array [8, 4, 2, 1] = 6 (Computed in O(N log N) time).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Cross Inversion Count**: When picking `R[j] < L[i]`, add `(mid - i + 1)` to inversion count.
2. **Recursive Sum**: Total inversions = left_inversions + right_inversions + split_inversions.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `count_inversions_merge_sort_demo()`: Solves Inversion Counting using Merge Sort in O(N log N) time.

projects.title: Quick Select Algorithm (Finding K-th Smallest Element in O(N) Avg)
projects.description: Quick Select finds the K-th smallest element in an unsorted array WITHOUT sorting the entire array! Uses QuickSort partitioning: if pivot index `pi == K-1`, return `arr[pi]`; if `pi > K-1`, recurse ONLY on left side; else recurse on right side. Solved in average `O(N)` time! In this project, you will build Quick Select Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Quick Select Selection Algorithm, Single-Branch Partition Recurrence & Average O(N) Time
projects.exampleText: Find 3rd smallest element in [7, 10, 4, 3, 20, 15] via Quick Select
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Quick Select Algorithm (K-th Smallest Element) ---
3rd Smallest Element in [7, 10, 4, 3, 20, 15] = 7 (Found in average O(N) time).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Partition**: Partition array using pivot index `pi`.
2. **Single Branch**: If `pi == k-1`, return `arr[pi]`. Recurse ONLY on matching side.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `quick_select_demo()`: Solves Quick Select algorithm to find K-th smallest element in average O(N) time.

projects.title: 3-Way Quick Sort (Dutch National Flag Partition for Duplicates)
projects.description: When an array contains heavy DUPLICATE keys, standard QuickSort degrades toward `O(N^2)`. 3-Way Quick Sort uses Dijkstra's Dutch National Flag algorithm to partition array into THREE regions: `< pivot`, `== pivot`, and `> pivot`. Runs in optimal `O(N)` time on duplicate arrays! In this project, you will build 3-Way Quick Sort in C.
projects.learningOutcome: 3-Way Dutch National Flag Partitioning, Heavy Duplicate Key Acceleration & Linear O(N) Speed
projects.exampleText: Partition array with heavy duplicate keys into 3 regions
projects.exampleOutput:
--- 3-Way Quick Sort (Dutch National Flag Partition) ---
Partitioned array with heavy duplicate keys into [< pivot, == pivot, > pivot] in O(N) time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **3 Pointers**: `lt` (less than), `i` (current), `gt` (greater than).
2. **3-Way Swaps**: Move `< pivot` elements to `lt`, `> pivot` elements to `gt`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `three_way_quicksort_demo()`: Solves 3-Way Quick Sort for heavy duplicate arrays.

projects.title: Tail Call Optimization in Quick Sort (O(log N) Call Stack Bound)
projects.description: Unbalanced QuickSort partitions can cause call stack overflow with `O(N)` stack frames! Optimize call stack depth to ALWAYS be `O(log N)` by recursing ONLY on the SMALLER partition, and using a tail-call while loop for the larger partition. In this project, you will build Tail Call Optimized Quick Sort in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Tail Call Stack Optimization, Logarithmic O(log N) Memory Bounds & Stack Overflow Guards
projects.exampleText: Bound QuickSort call stack depth to O(log N)
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Tail Call Optimization in Quick Sort ---
Guaranteed O(log N) call stack memory bound by recurring on smaller partition first.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Smaller Partition First**: Compare sizes of left and right partitions.
2. **Tail Call Loop**: Recurse on smaller partition; loop on larger partition.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `tail_call_quicksort_demo()`: Solves Tail Call Optimization in Quick Sort.

projects.title: External Merge Sort Engine for Disk File Chunk Sorting
projects.description: Sort huge datasets that do not fit into RAM memory (e.g. 100 GB file on a 4 GB RAM PC). Phase 1: Read RAM-sized chunks from disk, sort in-place, and write sorted run files to disk. Phase 2: K-Way Merge run files using a Min-Heap! In this project, you will build External Merge Sort Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: External Disk Memory Sorting, Run File Chunks & Min-Heap K-Way External Merging
projects.exampleText: Sort 100 GB file using 1 GB RAM chunks via external merge sort
projects.exampleOutput:
--- External Merge Sort Engine for Disk File Chunks ---
Sorted 100 GB disk dataset using 1 GB memory RAM chunks via k-way external merge.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Chunk Sorting**: Read RAM-capacity chunk, sort with QuickSort, save run file `run_i.bin`.
2. **External K-Way Merge**: Stream values from run files using Min-Heap into output file.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `external_merge_sort_demo()`: Solves External Merge Sort for huge disk datasets.

projects.title: Stable Merge Sort with Temporary Buffer Reuse
projects.description: Standard Merge Sort allocates temporary dynamic memory arrays `malloc()` inside every recursive call, causing severe heap allocation overhead. Allocate a SINGLE auxiliary array of size N upfront and reuse it across all recursive merge passes in `O(N log N)` time! In this project, you will build Buffer Reuse Merge Sort in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Heap Allocation Overhead Elimination, Buffer Reuse Patterns & Stable Sorting
projects.exampleText: Reuse single upfront auxiliary buffer across all merge passes
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Stable Merge Sort with Temporary Buffer Reuse ---
Allocated single O(N) scratch buffer upfront to eliminate dynamic malloc call overhead.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Upfront Allocation**: Allocate `int *scratch = malloc(N * sizeof(int))` once in main entry.
2. **Pass Scratch Pointer**: Pass `scratch` buffer to recursive `merge()` calls.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `buffer_reuse_merge_sort_demo()`: Solves Merge Sort with upfront buffer reuse.

projects.title: Dual-Pivot Quick Sort (Yaroslavskiy Scheme used in Java 7)
projects.description: Dual-Pivot Quick Sort selects TWO pivots `P1` and `P2` (`P1 <= P2`) and partitions array into THREE sub-ranges: `< P1`, `P1 .. P2`, and `> P2`. Performs faster than single-pivot QuickSort on modern CPU hardware (used in Java 7/8 `Arrays.sort()`). In this project, you will build Dual-Pivot Quick Sort in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Dual-Pivot Partitioning (Yaroslavskiy), Java Standard Library Sorters & CPU Cache Utilization
projects.exampleText: Partition array into 3 regions using 2 pivots P1 and P2
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Dual-Pivot Quick Sort (Yaroslavskiy Scheme) ---
Partitioned array into 3 regions using 2 pivots P1 and P2 (P1 <= P2).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Ensure P1 <= P2**: Swap `arr[low]` and `arr[high]` if `arr[low] > arr[high]`.
2. **3-Way Region Partition**: Partition elements relative to `P1` and `P2` simultaneously.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `dual_pivot_quicksort_demo()`: Solves Dual-Pivot Quick Sort.

projects.title: K-Way Merge Algorithm using Min-Heap / Priority Queue
projects.description: Given K sorted arrays of total N elements, merge them into a single sorted array. Insert first element of each array into a Min-Heap of size K. Repeatedly extract minimum element, append to output, and insert next element from same array in `O(N log K)` time! In this project, you will build K-Way Merge Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: K-Way Merging Mechanics, Min-Heap Priority Queues & O(N log K) Time Acceleration
projects.exampleText: Merge K=5 sorted arrays into 1 sorted output array
projects.exampleOutput:
--- K-Way Merge Algorithm using Min-Heap ---
Merged 5 sorted arrays into 1 sorted output array in O(N log K) time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Min-Heap Size K**: Insert `(val, array_idx, element_idx)` for K array heads.
2. **Extract & Advance**: Extract min, push to output, advance `element_idx` in original array.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `k_way_merge_demo()`: Solves K-Way Merge using Min-Heap.

projects.title: Reverse Pairs Counting via Extended Merge Sort
projects.description: Given an integer array nums, count total reverse pairs `(i, j)` where `i < j` and `nums[i] > 2 * nums[j]`. Extend Merge Sort: before merging two sorted halves `L` and `R`, use a two-pointer pass to count pairs satisfying `L[i] > 2 * R[j]` in `O(N log N)` time! In this project, you will build Reverse Pairs Counter in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Reverse Pairs Condition `nums[i] > 2 * nums[j]`, Extended Merge Sweeps & O(N log N) Counting
projects.exampleText: Count reverse pairs where nums[i] > 2 * nums[j]
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Reverse Pairs Counting via Extended Merge Sort ---
Counted reverse pairs (arr[i] > 2 * arr[j]) in O(N log N) time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Pre-Merge Counting**: Pointer `j` advances while `L[i] > 2 * R[j]`; add `(j - (mid + 1))` to total.
2. **Standard Merge**: Execute standard merge step after counting pass.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `reverse_pairs_demo()`: Solves Reverse Pairs counting using extended Merge Sort.

projects.title: Parallel Merge Sort using Multi-Threaded Recursive Splits
projects.description: Accelerate Merge Sort across multi-core processors using OpenMP parallel task directives `#pragma omp task`. Left and right subproblems execute concurrently on separate CPU threads when depth `< max_depth`, achieving linear multi-core speedup! In this project, you will build Parallel Merge Sort Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: OpenMP Multi-Threading Tasks, Parallel Subproblem Splits & Multi-Core Speedups
projects.exampleText: Execute parallel OpenMP merge sort across 4 CPU threads
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Parallel Merge Sort using Multi-Threaded Recursive Splits ---
Executed parallel OpenMP merge sort across 4 CPU threads.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Parallel Task Creation**: Use `#pragma omp task` for recursive `merge_sort` calls.
2. **Task Synchronization**: `#pragma omp taskwait` synchronizes before executing merge pass.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `parallel_merge_sort_demo()`: Solves Parallel Multi-Threaded Merge Sort using OpenMP.

projects.title: Quick Sort Worst-Case Killer Array Generator
projects.description: Demonstrate QuickSort vulnerabilities by constructing an adversary 'killer sequence' array that forces a deterministic QuickSort (e.g. picking middle element pivot) into its worst-case `O(N^2)` quadratic time behavior! In this project, you will build Quick Sort Killer Array Generator in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Adversarial Inputs Construction, QuickSort Vulnerabilities & Worst-Case Profiling
projects.exampleText: Generate adversary killer input forcing middle-pivot QuickSort into O(N^2) time
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Quick Sort Worst-Case Killer Array Generator ---
Generated adversary input forcing deterministic middle-pivot QuickSort into O(N^2) time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Adversary Construction**: Place largest elements at pivot inspection indices during recursive simulation.
2. **Quadratic Degeneration**: Forces partition sizes to be `1` and `N-1` at every recursion level.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `quick_sort_killer_demo()`: Generates Quick Sort worst-case killer arrays.

projects.title: Hybrid Quick-Insertion Sort with Cutoff Threshold
projects.description: Optimize QuickSort runtime by stopping recursion when subarray size `high - low + 1 <= CUTOFF` (typically 10 to 16). After QuickSort leaves the array nearly-sorted, execute a SINGLE Insertion Sort pass over the entire array in `O(N)` time! In this project, you will build Hybrid Quick-Insertion Sorter in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Production Hybrid Sorting Cutoffs, Cache Line Optimizations & Final Insertion Pass
projects.exampleText: Switch from QuickSort to InsertionSort for subarrays N <= 10
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Hybrid Quick-Insertion Sort with Cutoff Threshold ---
Switched from QuickSort to InsertionSort for subarrays of size N <= 10.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Subarray Cutoff**: Stop QuickSort recursion when `high - low + 1 <= 10`.
2. **Single Pass Insertion**: Run 1 Insertion Sort pass over array at the end.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `hybrid_quick_insertion_demo()`: Solves Hybrid Quick-Insertion Sort with cutoff threshold.

projects.title: IntroSort Kernel (Introspective Sort: QuickSort + HeapSort + InsertionSort)
projects.description: IntroSort (Introspective Sort) is the industry standard sorting algorithm used in C++ `std::sort`. Begins with QuickSort; switches to HeapSort if recursion depth exceeds `2 * log2(N)` (guaranteeing `O(N log N)` worst case); switches to InsertionSort for small subfiles `N <= 16`! In this project, you will build IntroSort Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: IntroSort Architecture (C++ `std::sort`), Max Recursion Depth Fallback & Guaranteed O(N log N)
projects.exampleText: Execute IntroSort combining QuickSort, HeapSort, and InsertionSort
projects.exampleOutput:
--- IntroSort Kernel (Introspective Sort) ---
Started with QuickSort; switched to HeapSort at max recursion depth 2*log(N); used InsertionSort for N<=16.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Depth Limit Guard**: If `depth_limit == 0`, switch to HeapSort.
2. **Small Subfile Cutoff**: If `N <= 16`, switch to InsertionSort.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `introsort_kernel_demo()`: Implements IntroSort (Introspective Sort) combining QuickSort, HeapSort, and InsertionSort.

projects.title: Parallel Multi-Threaded Quick Sort with Work-Stealing Task Queues
projects.description: High-throughput parallel sorting engines execute multi-threaded QuickSort using a Work-Stealing Task Queue pool. Idle worker threads steal partition tasks from busy worker queues, eliminating load imbalance on irregular partitions! In this project, you will build Work-Stealing Quick Sort Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Work-Stealing Task Queues, Dynamic Load Balancing & Parallel Partition Acceleration
projects.exampleText: Execute parallel quicksort partition tasks using work-stealing thread pools
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Parallel Multi-Threaded Quick Sort with Work-Stealing Task Queues ---
Evaluated parallel quicksort partition tasks using work-stealing thread pools.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Task Deque**: Each worker thread pushes sub-partition tasks to local double-ended queue.
2. **Work Stealing**: Idle threads steal tasks from tail of busy worker deques.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `work_stealing_quicksort_demo()`: Solves Parallel Quick Sort with work-stealing task queues.

projects.title: Block Merge Sort (In-Place O(1) Memory Stable Merge)
projects.description: Block Merge Sort achieves STABLE merge in optimal `O(N log N)` time using `O(1)` auxiliary space by breaking subarrays into square-root blocks of size `sqrt(N)` and sorting blocks via internal buffer swaps! In this project, you will build Block Merge Sort in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Block Merge Sort, O(1) Auxiliary Space Stable Merges & Square-Root Block Rotations
projects.exampleText: Execute stable merge in O(N log N) time using O(1) extra memory
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Block Merge Sort (In-Place O(1) Memory Stable Merge) ---
Executed stable merge in O(N log N) time using O(1) auxiliary RAM via block swaps.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Sqrt Block Partition**: Divide subarrays into internal blocks of size `sqrt(N)`.
2. **Block Swaps**: Use 1 block as internal buffer to stably merge adjacent blocks.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `block_merge_sort_demo()`: Solves Block Merge Sort in-place stable merge.

projects.title: SIMD Accelerated Lomuto Partition Kernel (256-bit AVX2)
projects.description: Accelerate QuickSort partitioning using 256-bit AVX2 SIMD vector instructions: compare 8 integer elements against pivot concurrently in 1 instruction pass using `_mm256_cmpgt_epi32()`! In this project, you will build SIMD Lomuto Partition Kernel in C.

projects.title: High-Throughput Memory-Mapped Telemetry File Chunk Sorter
projects.description: Telecommunication analytics engines sort 10,000,000 telemetry records per second by executing zero-copy QuickSort/MergeSort kernels directly over memory-mapped shared memory buffers (`mmap`). In this project, you will build Real-Time Telemetry Chunk Sorter in C.
